title and abstract.summary: The study analyzed historical records of plant species and Orthoptera (grasshoppers and crickets) to test how nitrogen deposition and plant richness changes influence the patterns of richness change of Orthoptera, taking into account Orthoptera species functional traits.

introduction.summary: The study investigated the relationships between Orthoptera species richness, plant species richness, and nitrogen deposition levels using data from the Netherlands.

results.summary: The study measured changes in species richness for Orthoptera and plants across different time periods and spatial scales in the Netherlands, examining relationships with ammonia deposition and food specialization. The study measured changes in species richness and related traits for the group Orthoptera across different spatial scales and environmental conditions.

discussion.summary: The study measured Orthoptera species richness across different time periods and spatial scales in the Netherlands, examining relationships with nitrogen deposition and plant species richness. The study examined the responses of Orthoptera species to changes in ammonia levels, comparing herbivorous and non-herbivorous groups, and also looked at the differences between grass specialists and generalists.
